items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We engaged a white drummer named Bob Haye but we had no bass.

ctx.x: Chit was in love with an Egyptian girl and had made arrangements with Pastraudis unbeknown to us to stay in Alexandria. He was satisfied to stay because of his love life, but I'm not certain if he was happy to have to work with us. The morale of this story was that someone had as much if not more power with the government administration than Pastraudis and I suppose he must have turned green when he found out that we have been permitted to remain in Alexandria after he had wanted us expelled. I never saw him…

We engaged a white drummer named Bob Haye but we had no bass. We also had to play for five acts, an Italian dance team, a Spanish dance team, a Hungarian dance team, a girl that did a Hula dance, one that danced Gypsy style and another that danced Spanish Flamenco style. Mae had sung with a trio for a while in Paris and she didn't have a bad voice. So she was engaged as singer. We had managed to recuperate the same appartment we had before. Our salary was the same as the one pound we had at the Monseigneur but…

The clientele at the Carlton was 100 per cent English and at that time the 'Lambeth Walk' song and dance was very popular. So for two months we had to play 'Lambeth Walk' at least three times a night.
